name: Booking.com
tagline: Global online travel agency for hotels, apartments, flights and car rentals.

pricing.plan: Free for travelers, commission-based for properties
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Booking.com is not software you pay for, it is a two-sided marketplace where millions of properties agree to be listed and pay commission on bookings. The website is the least interesting part: an agent could clone the search UI in an afternoon and it would return nothing, because there is no inventory behind it. Even if you scraped listings, you cannot hold rates, confirm availability, take a reservation, or make a hotel honor it. The consolation build is a personal trip shortlist tracker that you feed by hand, which is genuinely useful for comparing five candidate stays across dates without twelve browser tabs. Booking itself stays where it is.
coreLoopDIY: A local trip planner where you paste candidate stays with price, dates and link, then compare them side by side per trip and log which one you booked.
requirements: Manual entry of every stay you are considering, there is no inventory feed
whatYouLose: Actual bookable inventory: millions of properties with live availability and rates
Reservation confirmation, payment handling and cancellation flow
Review corpus from verified stays, which is the thing you actually read before booking
Loyalty pricing, genius discounts and bundled flight/car options
Customer support when the property says it has no record of you
moatNotes: Supply side signed contracts and connected their property management systems; demand side arrives from a decade of ad spend and SEO dominance. Neither half is code.
whyPeopleStillPay: Travelers do not pay Booking.com directly, so there is nothing to cancel. Properties pay commission because it delivers demand they cannot source themselves, and they keep paying because the alternative is empty rooms. For a traveler, the value is that one search box covers essentially every hotel on earth with a real cancellation policy behind it. No personal build touches that, because the asset is contracts and traffic, not a search interface.
notes: You can clone the search page in an afternoon and it will return exactly zero hotels. The moat is a few million signed supply contracts plumbed into live availability, plus the demand that makes signing them worth it.
prompt:
Build a local-first trip lodging shortlist tracker. Single Node project, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Node 20, Express, TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/trips.db
- Server-rendered EJS pages plus htmx for inline edits, no React, no build step beyond tsc
- Plain CSS in one stylesheet, dark theme, readable at 900px wide

Data model:
- trips: id, name, destination, start_date, end_date, budget_total, notes
- stays: id, trip_id, title, url, nightly_price, currency, total_price, check_in, check_out, guests, neighborhood, walk_notes, refundable (bool), rating_manual (1-5), status (candidate | shortlist | booked | rejected), created_at
- stays.total_price auto-computes from nightly_price and night count if left blank

Pages:
- / lists trips with dates and how many candidate stays each has
- /trips/:id shows a comparison table of stays: price per night, total, nights, refundable, your manual rating, status. Sortable by total and by price per night. Highlight anything over budget_total in red.
- Add-stay form on the trip page: paste a URL and fill the fields by hand. If the pasted URL has a hostname, store it and show the bare hostname as a label.
- Status buttons on each row (shortlist, booked, rejected) that patch in place via htmx
- One booked stay per trip max, enforced in the handler

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- Scraping any travel site, calling any hotel or OTA API, or fetching live rates
- Payments, reservations, or emailing anyone
- Auth, multi-user, hosting config

Include: npm scripts dev and start, schema migration on boot, a seed script with one example trip and three stays, and a README that says in the first line that this tracks stays you found elsewhere and books nothing. Put nothing in .env except PORT, and ship .env.example.
